results.title: PT Hartadinata Abadi Tbk (HRTA) to hold an extraordinary shareholders meeting on Oct 16 to seek approval for a 10% private placement
results.body: PT Hartadinata Abadi Tbk (HRTA) announced that it will convene an extraordinary shareholders meeting (RUPSLB) on Friday, 16 October 2026 to discuss a private placement (PMTHMETD). As the issuer, the company seeks approval to issue up to 10% of its capital, equivalent to 460,526,240 new shares. Only independent shareholders listed as of 23 September 2026 will be counted for quorum, and attendance must be confirmed via email with ID and written confirmation. On 24 September 2026, PT Hartadinata Abadi Tbk (HRTA) shares closed up 0.43% (10 points) at 2,310 after the meeting announcement.

results.title: PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) Stock Quietly Shorted
results.body: PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI), the issuer of the shares, fell 2.66% to Rp 4,070 on 24 September 2026 as foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 531.94 billion. Domestic brokers Mandiri Sekuritas and Stockbit Sekuritas together logged a net purchase of about Rp 221.4 billion, while trading volume reached 182.06 million shares (value Rp 748.06 billion). KB Valbury Sekuritas analyst Akhmad Nurcahyadi projects 3Q26 net profit of Rp 13.46 trillion (below consensus of Rp 13.97 trillion) and expects cumulative 9-month profit growth of 16.3% YoY, supported by 17.6% credit and DPK growth, 8.2% CASA increase, cost of credit 0.5%, and ROE 21.6%. The broker maintains a buy recommendation with a target price of Rp 5,660, implying a 2026 price-to-book ratio of 1.8x versus the current 1.4x.

results.title: Popular news roundup: Andy Hakim’s stake in PT Guna Timur Raya Tbk (TRUK), PT NexAI Digital Infrastruktur Tbk (MGLV)’s loan facility, PT Chandra Daya Investasi Tbk (CDIA)’s 22.8% revenue growth, PT Sinergi Inti Andalan Prima Tbk (INET)’s digital infrastructure expansion, and PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO), PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) and PT Arkora Hydro Tbk (ARKO) competing for green power supply to Singapore
results.body: The article compiles the day’s most popular financial news, covering several corporate actions. Hakimson Growth Capital bought 5 % (21.75 million shares) of PT Guna Timur Raya Tbk (TRUK) at Rp 428 per share, a total of about Rp 9.3 billion, well below the Rp 1,420 closing price on 18 September 2026. PT NexAI Digital Infrastruktur Tbk (MGLV) secured a loan facility from PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI) for its subsidiaries PT Nextier Askara Center (NAC) and PT Nextier GenAI Center (NGC) with a maximum commitment of Rp 4,125 trillion within an overall facility of Rp 10.75 trillion. PT Chandra Daya Investasi Tbk (CDIA) posted a 22.8 % year‑on‑year revenue increase to US$81.2 million in the first half of 2026, PT Sinergi Inti Andalan Prima Tbk (INET) is expanding its digital infrastructure business, and PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO), PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) and PT Arkora Hydro Tbk (ARKO) are competing to supply green electricity to Singapore from the Batam‑Bintan islands.

results.title: Foreign investors ramp up net selling, surpassing Rp 100 trillion
results.body: The article reports that foreign investors' net selling on the Indonesia Stock Exchange has exceeded Rp 100 trillion year‑to‑date, reaching Rp 104.3 trillion in the regular market. The biggest outflow was on PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) with a net sell of Rp 531.9 billion, followed by PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) at Rp 141.1 billion, while PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) recorded the largest net buy of Rp 24.4 billion. On Thursday 24 September 2026 the composite index (IHSG) closed down 76.3 points (‑1.2%) at 6,298.6, with total market turnover of Rp 11.2 trillion, as higher U.S. Treasury yields (10‑year >5%, 2‑year ≈4.9%) and a stronger dollar pressured Indonesian assets.

results.title: Foreign investors net sold a record Rp 1.49 trillion as the IHSG fell, with PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) topping the list of heavily shorted stocks.
results.body: Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 1.49 trillion across the Indonesian market on 24 September 2026, contributing to a 1.20 % decline in the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) to 6,298.60 points. The market saw 462 stocks close lower, total trading volume reach 29.03 billion shares worth Rp 10.82 trillion, and all sector indices weaken, the raw materials sector falling 2.17 % as the most corrected. The ten most heavily shorted stocks were PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) with a net sell of Rp 531.94 billion, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) Rp 133.24 billion, PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) Rp 84.61 billion, PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTM) Rp 51.65 billion, PT Darma Henwa Tbk (DEWA) Rp 39.70 billion, PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (TPIA) Rp 32.60 billion, PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN) Rp 32.03 billion, PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT) Rp 24.71 billion, PT Indosat Tbk (ISAT) Rp 24.02 billion, and PT Indika Energy Tbk (INDY) Rp 17.52 billion.

results.title: UOB Kay Hian recommends buy on PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) and hold on PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI), PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI) amid tighter funding conditions
results.body: UOB Kay Hian’s research notes that Indonesian banks are tightening funding strategies as liquidity remains constrained, and the broker maintains a buy rating on PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) while assigning hold to PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI), PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI). BBCA’s credit portfolio expanded 10.5% year‑on‑year to August 2026 with CASA growth of 10.8% YoY and a loan‑to‑deposit ratio of 81%, while BMRI’s credit grew 17.6% YoY, CASA rose 8.2% YoY and LDR reached 94.4% (potentially 101% excluding government SAL funds). BMRI relies heavily on non‑DPK funding, holding Rp 341 trillion in repo, interbank loans and securities (about 21% of its credit), compared with BBCA’s Rp 28 trillion (3% of credit), and Tier 1 capital ratios fell to 20.4% for BBRI (down 199 bps), 16.4% for BMRI (down 180 bps) and 15.5% for BBNI (down 270 bps) in the first half of 2026. The analyst notes that dividend payout ratios may be trimmed for BBRI and kept around 65% for BBNI in 2026, and that the banking sector remains cheap but UOB Kay Hian will monitor funding strength and capital adequacy before adjusting its stance.

results.title: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas recommends buy for major Indonesian banks amid retail credit pressure
results.body: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas (BRIDS) maintains buy recommendations for PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) (target price Rp 8,600), PT Bank BTPN Syariah Tbk (BTPS) (Rp 1,400), PT Bank CIMB Niaga Tbk (BNGA) (Rp 2,100), PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) (Rp 6,200), PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) (Rp 4,800), PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk (BRIS) (Rp 3,100), PT Bank Tabungan Negara Tbk (BBTN) (Rp 1,500) and PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) (not rated). The sector trades at roughly 1.5× price-to-book, about two standard deviations below its five-year average, while national credit expanded 13.65% yoy in August 2026, with investment credit growing 25.11% yoy, consumer credit growing 5.07% yoy, and consumer-related NPLs rising to 2.4-2.5% (KPR 3.3%, apartment 4.3%, vehicle 2.6%).

results.title: IHSG falls 1.20% to 6,298.61; analysts see support test at 6,200‑6,254 on Friday
results.body: The Indonesia Stock Exchange Composite Index (IHSG) closed down 1.20% at 6,298.61 on Thursday amid foreign‑investor selling of about Rp 987 billion, higher oil prices and rising US Treasury yields. Analysts highlighted support levels at 6,254 and 6,146 and resistance at 6,352 and 6,429, while also noting a potential test of the 6,186‑6,200 range with support at 6,200 and resistance at 6,400 on Friday. The index traded below its 5‑day and 100‑day moving averages, with MACD in negative territory and Stochastic RSI in oversold condition. The sell‑off targeted major bank stocks BMRI, BBRI and telecommunications firm TLKM, which were among the shares hit by foreign investors.

results.title: Technical stock recommendations for PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI), PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI), and PT Hartadinata Abadi Tbk (HRTA) for Friday (25/9).
results.body: The article issues technical trading recommendations for PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI), PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) and PT Hartadinata Abadi Tbk (HRTA) ahead of Friday, 25 September 2026. AADI closed at Rp 11,150 on Thursday, down 1.11% daily, with a speculative‑buy target supported at Rp 10,550 and resistance at Rp 11,750; BBRI closed at Rp 3,140, down 1.57%, with a buy entry suggested above Rp 3,150‑3,160, support at Rp 3,050 and resistance at Rp 3,320; HRTA closed at Rp 2,310, up 0.43%, trading above its MA10 of Rp 2,219 and with a buy‑on‑break recommendation at Rp 2,350, support at Rp 2,190 and resistance at Rp 2,500. The recommendations were provided by senior analysts Nafan Aji Gusta of Mirae Asset Sekuritas, Achmad Yaki of BCA Sekuritas and Oktavianus Audi of Kiwoom Sekuritas Indonesia. The broader market context showed the IHSG index ending at 6,298, down 1.20% with a total transaction value of Rp 11 trillion across 26.5 billion shares.

results.title: PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (INCO) reports operational recovery in Q2 2026 with higher nickel ore sales and matte production, prompting a new target price
results.body: PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (INCO), Indonesia’s largest nickel miner, is showing a gradual operational recovery in the second quarter of 2026, leading analysts to set a new target price for its shares. Nickel ore sales at the Bahodopi mine rose 21.3% quarter‑on‑quarter to 1.1 million wet metric tons, while sales from Pomalaa jumped to 496,000 wmt, almost four times the previous quarter. Nickel matte output increased 18.8% QoQ to 16.2 thousand tonnes, and the broker forecasts total matte production of 67.6 kt in 2026 and 71.0 kt in 2027. The implementation of the Harga Patokan Mineral (HPM) 363 policy is expected to boost INCO’s 2027 net profit by US$46 million, a 14.5% uplift, supported by integrated infrastructure and captive hydropower capacity of 365 MW.

results.title: Ubs Ag Ldn Branch A/C Client Sell Shares of Charoen Pokphand Indonesia
results.body: UBS AG London Branch A/C Client sold 4,046,633 CPIN shares at IDR 3,132 per share on 21 Sep 2026, a transaction worth IDR 12,674,054,556, reducing its stake to 983,483,167 shares (5.998% of CPIN) from 987,529,800 shares (6.022%). This sale follows two earlier disposals by the same client in September—3,541,747 shares at IDR 3,220 and 1,192,600 shares at IDR 3,111—indicating a continued reduction of its holding, now down by roughly 0.024 percentage points. The shares were sold to hedge the client’s derivatives trading activities.

results.title: Seven Indonesian banks report the highest net profits for the first half of 2026.
results.body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) posted a net profit of Rp31.18 trillion, up 17.5% YoY; PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) earned Rp30.41 trillion, up 24.4% YoY; PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) recorded Rp29.54 trillion, up 1.8% YoY; PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk posted Rp10.80 trillion, up 6.33% YoY; Bank Syariah Indonesia (BSI) reported Rp4.15 trillion, up 11.08% YoY; CIMB Niaga posted Rp3.43 trillion, down 2.2% YoY; and OCBC Indonesia posted Rp2.73 trillion, up 6.39% YoY. Credit disbursements expanded across the banks, with BRI reaching Rp1,580.42 trillion (UMKM 75.1% of the portfolio), Mandiri expanding to Rp1,592 trillion, BCA’s CASA reaching Rp1,082 trillion (84.3% of DPK) and credit of Rp1,036 trillion, BNI’s credit rising to Rp968.53 trillion, and CIMB Niaga’s credit growing 12.13% to Rp193.19 trillion, while BNI’s NPL stood at 1.9% and Mandiri’s at 0.98%. The strong earnings occurred in a macro environment of 5.3% GDP growth and 3.34% inflation. CIMB Niaga’s profit decline reflected pressure on interest margins despite a 25% rise in non‑interest income and an 87.22% jump in other income, whereas OCBC Indonesia’s results were supported by integration with the OCBC Group and growth in intermediation and cheap funding.

results.title: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) forecast to jump 38% and profit to soar 322%
results.body: In a research note dated 24 September 2026, Phintraco Sekuritas projects that PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) shares could rise about 38% and its net profit could surge roughly 322% by the end of 2026. The company reported Q2‑2026 revenue of US$746 million, up 11.7% quarter‑on‑quarter, and first‑half 2026 revenue of US$1.41 billion, 23.4% higher year‑on‑year. EBITDA increased 28.4% to US$455 million, while net profit jumped 208% to US$208 million, aided by a US$70.7 million (110.9% rise) contribution from associate PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN). Oil‑and‑gas output reached 170.1 mbopd, 19% above the prior period and above the FY26 guidance of 165‑170 mbopd, driven by a 24% increase in participation rights in Block Corridor and new production from the Forel and Terubuk projects.

results.title: Choosing Stocks with the Highest Interim Dividends for 2026 – Full List
results.body: The article presents a list of Indonesian issuers that have announced interim dividends for the first half of 2026, highlighting those with the most generous payouts. PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) will distribute an interim dividend of Rp3.07 triliun, representing 10% of its semester‑I net profit of Rp29.5 triliun, and analysts set a target price of Rp8,075. PT Chandra Daya Investasi Tbk (CDIA) announced an interim payout ratio of 58%, while Emiten Prajogo Pangestu disclosed a dividend of US$10 juta (approximately Rp1.42 per saham). Other issuers noted for attractive interim yields include BMRI, CMRY, BSSR (with a payout around 95%) and BPII (with a payout about 82% despite a 53% YoY profit decline). Analysts caution that high interim payouts may strain cash flow for capital‑intensive firms, recommending investors consider sustainability of earnings and cash generation alongside dividend yields.

results.title: Maybank Sekuritas sees 27.1% credit growth and maintains a buy rating for PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI)
results.body: PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI) posted a 27.1% year‑on‑year increase in credit to Rp 977 trillion in August 2026, the strongest growth among banks. Maybank Sekuritas Indonesia keeps a buy recommendation with a target price of Rp 4,800 per share, based on a projected 2026 price‑to‑book ratio of 1.0× and a current valuation of 0.8× P/BV. Net profit rose to Rp 14.3 trillion (up 6.9% YoY) supported by a 14.3% rise in net interest income, while net interest margin fell to 3.1% and provisions climbed 26.9% YoY, highlighting margin pressure and higher funding costs. Deposits grew 29.4% YoY to Rp 1,125 trillion, improving the loan‑to‑deposit ratio to 86.9% but reducing the CASA share to 65.3%, indicating a shift toward more expensive funding sources.

results.title: Bank Indonesia Holds BI Rate at 5.75% and Panin Sekuritas Lists PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI), PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA), PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI), and PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) as Top Buy Picks.
results.body: On 23 September 2026 the Rapat Dewan Gubernur Bank Indonesia kept the BI Rate at 5.75% with the deposit facility at 4.75% and the lending facility at 6.5%. The spread between the BI Rate and the U.S. Fed rate narrowed to 1.75% from 2% and August bank credit growth rose 13.65% year‑on‑year, supporting a positive outlook for interest‑rate‑sensitive stocks. Panin Sekuritas highlighted PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI), PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA), PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) and PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) as its top buy recommendations, assigning 12‑month target prices of Rp3,856, Rp8,157, Rp5,221 and Rp4,384 respectively. Analyst consensus shows strong buying interest, with 23 analysts recommending BBRI, 35 for BBCA, 29 for BMRI and 24 for BBNI, reflecting expectations of continued credit expansion and a stable rupiah.

results.title: ADRO, MEDC, and ARKO Compete for Green Power Export to Singapore
results.body: The three issuers PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO), PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) and PT Arkora Hydro Tbk (ARKO) are competing to become Singapore’s green electricity supplier from the Batam‑Bintan islands. ADRO, through its subsidiary Adaro Solar International, has secured a 0.4 GW allocation from the Singapore regulator and plans a US$3.2 billion capital expenditure for the project. MEDC, via the Pacific Medco Solar Energy consortium with Grup Salim, obtained conditional approval for 600 MW within a 2 GWp Batam solar PV project. ARKO’s subsidiary Endorshine Energy Solutions received US$9.8 million financing from PT Sarana Multi Infrastruktur for a commercial PLTS project, positioning ARKO as a potential dark‑horse contender.

results.title: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) Facilitates 5,000 Halal Certifications for UMKM and Posts 13% YoY Net Profit Growth in August 2026
results.body: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) is facilitating roughly 5,000 halal certifications for micro, small and medium enterprises (UMKM) through its Workshop Sertifikasi Halal program that began in 2023. The initiative, which includes business model canvas training, aims to boost UMKM competitiveness and has coincided with an average 8.5% revenue increase for certified UMKM according to Ministry data. In August 2026, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) reported net profit of Rp4.9 trillion, up 13% year‑on‑year and down 3% month‑to‑month, while net profit for the first eight months reached Rp40.2 trillion, 3% higher YoY and representing 67% of consensus estimates. Net interest income grew 8% YoY, credit expanded 2% month‑to‑month to Rp1,018 trillion (11% YoY) and credit cost stayed at 0.3%, below the 0.4‑0.5% guidance for 2026.

results.title: Two PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) executives, Prijono Sugiarto and Rudy, make insider purchases, with Rudy acquiring about Rp21.14 billion of ASII shares
results.body: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) disclosed that two senior executives increased their shareholdings through direct market purchases. Komisaris Utama Prijono Sugiarto bought 8,700 shares at Rp4,850 each on 21 September 2026, spending about Rp42.19 million and raising his stake from 5,587,100 to 5,595,800 shares (0,0138% of the company). Director Rudy accumulated 4.4 million shares in two stages—2.2 million at Rp4,820 on 21 September and another 2.2 million at Rp4,790 on 22 September—totaling roughly Rp21.14 billion. His holding grew from 1.2 million to 5.6 million shares, also representing about 0,0138% of voting rights, marking a significant insider stake increase.

results.title: IHSG projected to weaken on 24 Sept; BNI Sekuritas recommends six stocks
results.body: BNI Sekuritas' head of retail research, Fanny Suherman, expects the Indonesia Composite Index (IHSG) to face another correction on 24 Sept, with support around 6,320‑6,340 and resistance near 6,420‑6,440 after the index closed up 1.56% at 6,374.91 on 23 Sept amid a net foreign sell of Rp 468 billion. The brokerage issued speculative‑buy recommendations for six stocks: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) with entry 1,450‑1,465, stop‑loss below 1,450 and target 1,480‑1,500; PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) entry 2,570‑2,600, stop‑loss below 2,570, target 2,620‑2,660; PT Triputra Agro Persada Tbk (TAPG) entry 1,940‑1,980, stop‑loss below 1,940, target 2,030‑2,060; PT MNC Tourism Indonesia Tbk (KPIG) entry 55, stop‑loss below 54, target 57‑60; PT Astrindo Nusantara Infrastruktur Tbk (BIPI) entry 147‑150, stop‑loss below 146, target 155‑160; and PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) entry 935‑960, stop‑loss below 920, target 980‑1,020. The recommendations come as foreign investors sold BBRI, BMRI, TLKM, ISAT and ADRO, with ADRO also appearing among the picks. BNI Sekuritas positions these six stocks as speculative opportunities ahead of the anticipated IHSG pull‑back.

results.title: Bank Rakyat Indonesia (BBRI) announces limited review and upcoming publication of its Q3‑2026 financial statements
results.body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) disclosed that its consolidated financial statements for the period ending 30 September 2026 will undergo a limited review by a public accountant and will be published in accordance with applicable regulations. In the first half of 2026, BRI and its subsidiaries reported a net profit of Rp30.86 trillion, up 17.42 % YoY, driven by a 5.42 % increase in interest income to Rp107.92 trillion and a 5.87 % decline in interest expense to Rp27.39 trillion, yielding net interest income of Rp80.53 trillion (+9.91 %) while impairment provisions rose 9.64 % to Rp25.51 trillion. Profitability ratios improved, with pre‑tax ROA at 3.30 %, after‑tax ROA at 2.70 % and ROE at 22.59 %, although the net interest margin fell to 6.40 % from 6.58 %, reflecting broader banking‑sector margin pressures.

results.title: PT Elang Mahkota Teknologi Tbk (EMTK) strengthens its position in PT Bukalapak.com Tbk (BUKA) and PT Nitrasanata Dharma Tbk (JECX)
results.body: The BEI disclosed on 22 Sep that PT Elang Mahkota Teknologi Tbk (EMTK) increased its holdings in PT Bukalapak.com Tbk (BUKA) by 188.70 million shares, raising its stake to 10.67%, and added 1.17 million shares of PT Nitrasanata Dharma Tbk (JECX) through its health subsidiary PT Sarana Meditama Metropolitan Tbk (SAME), bringing its total shareholdings to 33%. PT Yulie Sekuritas Indonesia Tbk (YULE) raised its stake in PT Esa Medika Mandiri Tbk (EMMI) to about 10.19%; Samudra (Investment) Pte. Ltd boosted its holding in PT Mitra Adiperkasa Tbk (MAPI) to 30.19%; and Lo Kheng Hong increased his position in PT Intiland Development Tbk (DILD) to 7.54%. Edwin Soeryadjaya now controls 35.95% of PT Saratoga Investama Sedaya Tbk (SRTG), Ferry Sudjono holds roughly 6.02% of PT Fore Kopi Indonesia Tbk (FORE), while Dato Tahir reduced his stake in PT Maha Properti Indonesia Tbk (MPRO) to 10.46%. PT Global Mediacom Tbk (BMTR) sold 28.90 million shares of its subsidiary PT Media Nusantara Citra Tbk (MNCN), lowering its control to 38.23%, and The Bank of New York Mellon divested 6 million shares of PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (TLKM), retaining about 6.3% of the telecom firm.

results.title: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) and PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) lead foreign net sell list as IHSG rebounds.
results.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) rebounded on Wednesday, closing at 6,374.91, up 97.86 points (1.56%). Despite the market gain, foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp461.35 billion across the market, with 448 stocks advancing, 186 declining and 159 unchanged. The ten stocks with the largest foreign net sell were PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) (Rp187.64 bn), PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) (Rp128.73 bn), PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) (Rp124.67 bn), PT Indosat Tbk (ISAT) (Rp66.49 bn), PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) (Rp45.77 bn), PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI) (Rp35.30 bn), PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) (Rp31.01 bn), PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk (CPIN) (Rp28.87 bn), PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) (Rp28.27 bn), and PT AKR Corporindo Tbk (AKRA) (Rp20.33 bn). Total trading volume reached 36.09 billion shares with a transaction value of Rp12.54 trillion.

results.title: IHSG rises 1.56% to 6,374.91 as foreign investors net buy ten leading stocks
results.body: The Indonesia Composite Index (IHSG) closed up 97.86 points, or 1.56%, at 6,374.91 on Wednesday, with all sector indices in the green. Trading involved 448 advancing, 186 declining and 159 unchanged stocks, a total volume of 36.09 billion shares and IDR 12.54 trillion in transactions, while foreign investors posted a net sell of IDR 461.35 billion. Despite the net outflow, foreign investors were net buyers of ten stocks: PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) – IDR 106.73 billion; PT Timah Tbk (TINS) – IDR 53.70 billion; PT Singaraja Putra Tbk (SINI) – IDR 40.85 billion; PT Pertamian Geothermal Energy Tbk (PGEO) – IDR 27.70 billion; PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (TPIA) – IDR 26.26 billion; PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (INCO) – IDR 23.45 billion; PT Indika Energy Tbk (INDY) – IDR 23.05 billion; PT Triputra Agro Persada Tbk (TAPG) – IDR 19.17 billion; PT VKTR Teknologi Mobilitas Tbk (VKTR) – IDR 17.90 billion; and PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN). The strongest sector gains were in basic materials (+3.47%), energy (+2.59%) and consumer cyclical (+2.49%).

results.title: PT Sinergi Inti Andalan Prima Tbk (INET) and PT Solusi Sinergi Digital Tbk (WIFI) launch a 6,870‑km submarine cable project linking Jakarta and Sorong
results.body: The consortium led by PT Sinergi Inti Andalan Prima Tbk (INET) and PT Solusi Sinergi Digital Tbk (WIFI) has initiated the development of the SGI Cable System, a 6,870‑km submarine cable linking Jakarta with Sorong. SGI (PT Sarana Global Indonesia), a subsidiary 60% owned by INET, will act as developer and operator, and the project targets Ready for Service by the end of 2028 after a memorandum of understanding was signed on 23 September 2026. The cable will feature 16 fiber‑pair routes delivering up to 25 Tbps capacity across 14 landing points, with a design life of 25 years; PT FiberHome Technologies Indonesia expects to deliver all required materials by September 2027, Nokia Indonesia will provide high‑capacity optical network technology, and NTT Group, through PT Integrasi Jaringan Ekosistem (Weave), will supply backbone network and capacity distribution. INET will use the capacity as a majority shareholder, while WIFI (via its Surge brand) and other consortium members will also draw capacity to support expanding broadband, data‑center, cloud and AI services across Indonesia.

results.title: ADMR Stock Stagnates Amid Strong H1 2026 Earnings, Analysts Point to Aluminium Expansion as Needed Catalyst
results.body: PT Alamtri Minerals Indonesia Tbk (ADMR) saw its share price close at Rp 1,560 on 23 September, a modest 2.63% gain that leaves the stock essentially stagnant for the year despite solid financial results. In the first half of 2026 the company posted revenue of US$584 million, up 39.3% YoY, and net profit of US$174.2 million, up 24% YoY, with mining product sales accounting for 99.6% of revenue and no aluminium contribution yet. Analysts from Mirae Asset Sekuritas and Phintraco Sekuritas argue that the market awaits proof that ADMR’s aluminium downstream expansion, pursued through PT Kalimantan Aluminium Industry and targeted to generate revenue from H2 2026 onward with a 500,000‑ton smelter capacity, can offset coal‑related volatility. Both firms maintain buy recommendations, setting target prices of Rp 2,310 and an entry range of Rp 1,505‑1,595 respectively.

results.title: Cermati recommends buying PT Alamtri Minerals Indonesia Tbk (ADMR) amid solid first‑half 2026 performance
results.body: PT Alamtri Minerals Indonesia Tbk (ADMR) posted first‑half 2026 revenue of US$584 million, up 39.3% YoY, with gross profit of US$227.8 million (gross margin 47.6%) and net profit of US$174.2 million, a 24% YoY rise, while metallurgical coal sales volume grew 9% and the aluminium smelter operated by PT Kalimantan Aluminium Industry is expected to generate revenue from the second half of 2026. Mirae Asset Sekuritas and Phintraco Sekuritas both maintain buy ratings, citing the strong fundamentals and an entry range of Rp 1,505–1,595 (target price Rp 2,310) as the stock rose 2.63% to Rp 1,560 on 23 Sept 2026.

results.title: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas issues stock recommendations for HRTA, VKTR and PGEO on Thursday, 24 September 2026
results.body: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas recommended three stocks—HRTA, VKTR and PGEO—for trading on Thursday, 24 September 2026. HRTA’s price rebounded from a support zone of 2,100‑2,150, broke above the 20‑day moving average of 2,230 and the 200‑day moving average of 2,260, with a MACD turning positive, and the broker sees upside to 2,360‑2,475 while the company plans a private placement of up to 460.5 million new shares (≈10% of equity) ahead of an independent shareholders meeting on 16 October 2026. VKTR recovered from a Fibonacci support range of 729‑663, moved above the 200‑day moving average of 794 and, despite a still‑negative MACD, shows a potential rise to 855‑915, and the firm signed a non‑binding term sheet with BNBR and Danantara Investment Management on 1 September to explore strategic investment in a commercial electric‑vehicle ecosystem. PGEO broke out above the neckline at 1,070, stayed above the 200‑day moving average of 1,052 and formed a cup‑and‑handle pattern with a bullish MACD crossover, giving a target of 1,113‑1,140, while the company secured US$477.8 million of international funding for three geothermal projects and reported a roughly 40 % year‑on‑year profit increase in Q1 2026.

results.title: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) shares see net foreign sell offset by domestic buying, closing up 0,31%
results.body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) shares recorded a net foreign sell of Rp 187.64 miliar on 23/9/2026, while domestic investors posted a net buy of Rp 187.6 miliar. Based on data from Stockbit Sekuritas, domestic investors net bought Rp 187.6 miliar, with Stokcbit Sekuritas (Rp 30.5 miliar), CGS International Sekuritas (Rp 26.7 miliar) and BCA Sekuritas (Rp 23.8 miliar) contributing, helping the stock close up 0.31% at Rp 3,190. For semester I‑2026 the bank reported PATMI of Rp 31.2 triliun, a 17.5% yoy increase, with net interest income up 9.9%, pre‑provision operating profit up 12.8%, cost of credit improving to 3.1%, total credit rising 16.2% yoy to Rp 1,645.5 triliun (corporate credit +47.1%, commercial credit +58.1%) and the micro‑credit portfolio at Rp 714.1 triliun, while gross NPL fell to 2.90% and loan at risk (LAR) improved to 9.1%. Kiwoom Sekuritas Indonesia maintains a buy recommendation with a 12‑month target price of Rp 4,000, implying a P/BV of 1.8 kali versus a three‑year average of 2.06 kali, while flagging risks from prolonged NIM pressure, tighter liquidity, slower credit growth, higher cost of credit and delayed micro‑asset quality recovery.

results.title: Foreign Investors Pull Back, Leading Stocks See Heavy Selling
results.body: Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 461.3 billion across the Indonesian market on Wednesday, 23 September 2026, while the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) rose 97.87 points (1.56%) to 6,374.9 at the close. The largest foreign outflows were in PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) with a net sell of Rp 187.6 billion, followed by BMRI with Rp 128.7 billion, TLKM with Rp 124.6 billion, and PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) with Rp 35.3 billion. In total, foreign investors sold Rp 468.2 billion in the regular market, while net buying in the negotiation and cash market amounted to Rp 6.9 billion. Overall market turnover reached Rp 12.8 trillion, with 464 stocks rising, 200 falling and 299 unchanged.
